fields.title: Veer: mobile signup conversion is three times worse
fields.summary: Marketing demands a overhaul of mobile signup. Decide what to do in two weeks.
fields.decisionPrompt: What will you do in two weeks?
fields.brief/role: You are the product manager for signup and activation.
fields.brief/company: Veer is a fictional 60-person company selling accounting software to small businesses.
fields.brief/context: Marketing bought more mobile traffic this quarter and noticed: on mobile, 11% of visitors reach signup completion vs 34% on desktop. The CMO asked engineering to 'fix mobile signup' and put the overhaul in the quarterly plan. Nobody looked at the step-by-step funnel. The CTO asked you to investigate before the team spends a sprint.
fields.brief/objective: Understand where people are dropping off and decide what to do.
fields.brief/constraints: One developer and one designer are available for two weeks. Analytics tracking on mobile was installed later than desktop and has known gaps.
fields.brief/task: Choose what to do and justify it.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: 'Fix mobile signup' is not a task
fields.learnTakeaway/body: A gap between devices is almost never spread evenly across the funnel: it sits at a single step, and finding it takes an hour. What matters next is the root cause: a broken redirect takes four days to fix, whereas moving the step would destroy activation, because that step drives it. Demands framed as 'overhaul everything' must be translated into a specific step and root cause before a team spends a sprint.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content:
Visitors reaching signup page, by step completion.

Desktop: page 100% → email 71% → password 66% → company details 58% → bank connection 41% → account created 34%.

Mobile: page 100% → email 64% → password 60% → company details 49% → bank connection 13% → account created 11%.

Up to 'bank connection', the drop-off difference per step is small. At this step, desktop loses 29% of remaining users, mobile loses 73%.

Mobile tracking lacks return events from bank website: a known gap.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content:
Designer reviewed 22 mobile sessions that reached bank connection.

14 sessions: user taps 'Connect bank', gets redirected to bank page, session ends there. No return. In several, user scrolls bank page for 20–40 seconds.

5 sessions: user taps 'Skip' — a small text link under the button — and completes signup.

3 sessions: user taps 'Connect bank', returns, sees an empty form with lost input, and leaves.

On desktop, none of the reviewed sessions ended on the bank page.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content:
Support receives ~30 tickets per month saying: 'tried signing up on mobile, sent me to bank, then nothing happened.'

Sales note: accounts connecting bank during signup activate 3x higher and churn significantly less in first 90 days. Revenue team defends this step and previously blocked moving it post-signup.

Marketing note: mobile traffic is 46% of total and growing.

Mobile acquisition cost is 20% lower than desktop.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content:
From conversation with a developer:

'There are two separate things here, constantly conflated.

1) The bank redirect was built for desktop. On mobile browsers, the return URL opens in a new tab in some versions, leaving the original tab with an incomplete form — user thinks "nothing happened". Vendor has an SDK handling this; switching takes ~4 days.

2) Position of "Skip" link is a UI tweak, half a day. Currently smaller than button and below the fold on small screens.

Complete signup overhaul has nothing to do with these two items.'
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Fix bank return redirect and move 'Skip' link up
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Switch to vendor SDK so return redirect works on mobile, and fix 'Skip' link positioning.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence:
Step-by-step analysis shows that the drop before connecting a bank is small: 49% vs 58%. That means 'mobile registration' as a whole isn't broken—a single step is.
Recordings explain which one: 14 out of 22 sessions end on the bank page, and the developer names the reason—the return flow opens in a new tab.
Four days for the library and half a day for the link. Two weeks later, step completion from phone rises from 13% to 31%, registration from 11% to 26%.
Thirty requests a month about 'sent to bank and nothing happened' stop.
The step stays in registration, so the revenue department loses nothing: the three times better activation among those who connected a bank remains.
Trade-off: the quarterly item about redesigning stays on the plan, and you bring its cancellation with numbers, not an opinion.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Spend two weeks on mobile analytics tracking to trust the numbers before deciding what to build.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence:
Caution is justified: bank return events are missing, and that's the problematic step.
However, two weeks are spent measuring what is already clear: 14 of 22 recordings end on bank page, developer knows root cause and estimated 4 days.
After fixing tracking, numbers confirm the exact picture, and actual fix starts two weeks late.
Meanwhile, mobile traffic (46% of total) continues dropping off at that step.
Trade-off: gained precision where direction was already clear; though fixed tracking helps later, it delayed resolution.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Move bank connection out of signup flow
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Complete signup without bank, offer connection on first login — remove the step where most mobile users drop off.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence:
Mobile signup immediately rises from 11% to around 30%: the step that was losing 73% is gone.
But a month later, something else is clear: the share of users connecting a bank in the first week drops from 41% to 22%, and such accounts activate three times more often and churn less in the first 90 days.
The revenue department brings this up at a meeting, having blocked this proposal before.
Yet the cause of the drop was not the step itself, but a broken return flow: four days of work brought back both the step and the conversion.
Trade-off: the registration metric improved at the cost of activation, even though choosing between them was not required.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Accept quarterly roadmap item as given and spend two weeks initiating full mobile flow overhaul.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence:
Two weeks spent on wireframes and initial screens.
Funnel analysis would have shown gap before bank step was only 9 percentage points, but 28 at bank step: only one step needed fixing.
Overhaul will take a full quarter; meanwhile 46% of traffic continues dropping on broken redirect fixable in 4 days.
After a quarter, new signup launches but contains the same bank redirect issue because nobody updated the vendor library.
Trade-off: accepted stakeholder request at face value without looking at the step-by-step funnel.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Channel chosen by popularity rather than intent and testable bet
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Acquisition cost evaluated by leads, without conversion to payment or payback
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Bottleneck identified by lowest percentage rather than highest leverage
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Failed to find the action after which churn stops
fields.rubric/remediation/4/gap: Retention mechanic does not match the natural frequency of the task
fields.rubric/remediation/5/gap: Differentiation defined as 'better at everything', which means nothing
